name: Side bend
pattern: Lateral flexion: the trunk bends sideways and back up against a load, or curls sideways on the floor (side crunch, heel touches). Windmills add a hip hinge.
setup: Stand tall, feet hip width, a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Other hand on your hip or behind your head.

steps.text: Bend sideways toward the weight, sliding it down the outside of your thigh.
Stop at a comfortable stretch, no twisting or leaning forward.
Pull yourself back to upright with the opposite side, then a little past.

cues.cue: Bend straight sideways, like between two panes of glass.
cues.why: Pure side bending targets the obliques and quadratus lumborum; mixing in twist or forward bend changes the load.
End-range lateral bending raises the load on spine tissues.

cues.cue: One weight only; the other hand is free.
cues.why: Weights in both hands cancel each other out.

cues.cue: Hips stay still; the movement is above the belt.
cues.why: Shifting the hips sideways hides the trunk bend.

breathing: Breathe in as you bend, out as you come up.

tempo.note: About 2 s down and 2 s up.

mistakes.name: Twisting or leaning forward
mistakes.looks: The shoulders rotate or the chest drops forward as you bend.
mistakes.why: It turns the bend into a loaded twist or flexion.

mistakes.name: Hips slide sideways
mistakes.looks: The hips push out away from the weight while the trunk stays straight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips over the feet.

mistakes.name: Jerking up
mistakes.looks: Fast bounce out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Slow down; pause briefly at the bottom.
mistakes.why: Momentum loads the spine at end range.

safety: Low back pain: try a side plank first; it trains the same muscles with less spine load.
Windmills: only with good hip hinge and shoulder mobility; keep the arm vertical and eyes on the weight.

variants.change: Side-lying on a 45 degree bench: the trunk lowers and lifts sideways against gravity.
Lying on the floor: a small sideways curl of the ribs toward the hip.
Weight overhead, hips push sideways and hinge down: also a hip-hinge and shoulder-stability drill.

subtypes.name: Side crunch and heel touches
subtypes.change: Lying on your back with knees bent (heel touches) or on your side; reach one hand toward the same-side heel with a small sideways curl.

subtypes.name: Windmill
subtypes.change: Weight locked overhead in the right hand, feet angled left; push the hips right and hinge down until the left hand reaches the left foot.

motion.basis: Default is the standing dumbbell side bend, weight in the right hand. The convention has no trunk side-bend key: the rig needs one (about 25-30 degrees at the bottom, estimate); here only the arms, scapula and hips show the change. All angles estimated.
